questions.q: Why do you need Node.js installed if your browser already runs JavaScript?
options: This course writes standalone scripts, installs packages, and eventually talks to a live blockchain from the command line — none of which runs inside a browser tab
Browsers cannot actually run JavaScript at all
Node.js replaces the need for a browser entirely
Node.js is only needed for writing HTML
questions.explain: Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser as a standalone program, which is required for scripts, packages, and command-line blockchain work.

questions.q: On the nodejs.org download page, which option should you choose for this course?
options: LTS (Long-Term Support)
Current
Whichever one downloads faster
Neither — download from a third-party mirror instead
questions.explain: LTS is the stable, recommended release channel; Current is the bleeding-edge version not recommended for learners.

questions.q: After installing Node.js, which two terminal commands confirm the install worked?
options: node -v and npm -v
node install and npm install
node --start and npm --start
node run and npm run
questions.explain: Both commands print a version number back when Node.js and npm are correctly installed.

questions.q: What does it mean if your terminal says "node is not recognized" after installing Node.js?
options: The installer likely didn't finish, or the terminal was opened before the install completed — closing and reopening a fresh terminal usually fixes it
Node.js was installed correctly and this message is expected
JavaScript itself is broken on your machine
You must reinstall Windows entirely
questions.explain: A fresh terminal picks up the updated system PATH set by the installer; an already-open one won't see it.

questions.q: What editor does this course assume you're using for every lesson, and why?
options: VS Code — a free Microsoft code editor with a built-in terminal, so you never have to leave it to run commands
Notepad, because it requires no setup
A web-based online compiler only
Microsoft Word, since it has a built-in spell checker
questions.explain: VS Code's integrated terminal runs the same commands (like node -v) directly inside the editor.
